I wanted a USB-chargeable pocket razor to use on my face while in the hospital. I especially liked that the WIOR Razor was listed as washable, and that the photos in the listing even included one showing a hand holding the razor under a stream of water.

The razor is nicely boxed, but I noted the unit itself was quite light compared to other travel razors about the same size I've used in recent years (my favorite one is no longer available in America, alas). Still, a lighter razor is no big deal, as long as it works.

I read the instruction leaflet - only to immediately see a warning not to expose the razor to water! ( ¿ ?) I double checked the Amazon listing to make sure I was sent the right razor, and I certainly was - however, the depiction of it as washable - particularly the image of someone holding it under a faucet stream - is highly misleading. One must remove the foil screen frame and then pull of the cutter block (while being careful the tiny spring does not fall out), and then wash the block separately.

I quickly phoned Amazon's product support number, to explain the major discrepancy, as was told measures would bet taken to correct the listing so no one else would be mislead. I had the option of returning the razor, but given my immediate need, decided to keep it.

It worked reasonably well the first week or so, but the cutter block quickly dulled and shaving became a bit painful over the course of the next couple weeks. I certainly did carefully wash the cutter block by removing the foil in its frame, and then pulling off the block (and each time the little spring would pop off, but fortunately was never lost). However, by last week, just 32 days after purchase, the shaver was cutting quite poorly - even causing a bit of pain to use. In only a month, with light use, the cutting block had dulled to the point of uselessness.

I must point out that despite my call about the misleading product description and imagery, the washability feature remains in the listing as of this writing, five weeks later.

I got the 22” Body Wave 13x4 T Part Lace.

I do NOT recommend this wig! I recommend you quickly exit out from looking at this one and find ANYTHING else! The hair is so fried! It looks and feels unhealthy! The knots are HUUUUGE! They look sooo unnatural! The top is thin so you can see the tracks. Since you only have 1” parting space, which is already the middle part, there’s no room to change it so you can’t even try to cover the tracks. There are stains inside the cap, which look to be from the combs. There are tons of dark hairs mixed throughout the hair (even though the product page said it was virgin hair, unprocessed hair. But this definitely did not come from a natural blonde. It was bleached and it wasn’t done well so it’s totally fried!). I would honestly give it zero stars if I could, but I have to give at least 1 star. I go into more detail below if you’re interested…

The product page states this is 150% density. I’m never good at determining if it’s accurate density. It honestly looks about 150% density. HOWEVER, there are areas on the top that are thin and you clearly see the tracks. Unfortunately, this is a T part Lace, so you don’t have room to change the part to cover the thin area. To me, that makes it unbearable.

The knots on this thing are INSANE! I have no clue what on earth is going on with them but they are HUGE!! They look so unnatural and ridiculous!

The product page says it is “premium hair material” and “we guarantee that T part Blonde 613 Lace Front Wig Human Hair Is 100% Real Blonde Human Hair Wigs, Soft & Healthy, No Tangle, No Shedding, Can Be Dyed, Bleached, Curled Etc.; You Can Buy without Worries.” Honestly, that is a joke! It is blonde, but it has been processed to be blonde. There are a ton of dark hairs mixed in throughout the hair. The hair has been badly bleached so it’s fried. I would never want to dye/bleach this again because I honestly don’t think the hair could take it since it’s in such bad condition! It definitely isn’t “healthy.” It’s not even really all that soft because you can feel how the hair is fried.

The hair they show on the mannequins in the product photos on the product page are definitely NOTHING like the hair I received! That hair looks soft, healthy, plucked well, and without humongous knots and tracks showing on top.

When you scroll down to the middle of the product page where they have more info. It says on the side in the grey box, “Wig Type: T Part Blonde Body Wave Virgin Human Hair Wigs.” It also says, “ Human Hair Quality: Unprocessed Brazilian Human Hair, Minimum Shedding.” “Just Like Your Own Human Hair, No Chemical.” Just full of LIES! This is NOT virgin hair. Virgin hair is also known as unprocessed hair (they mean the same thing). Unprocessed hair is human hair that has NEVER been chemically processed, this means over the life of the hair it’s never been dyed, coloured, or bleached. As a result, unprocessed hair is incredibly healthy. This has DEFINITELY been bleached so it is NOT Virgin/unprocessed. It is definitely NOT “no chemical.”

It has 13x6x1 T part lace. That means the lace goes 13” in the front ear to ear, it goes 6 inches back, and the parting space is 1”. The product page said, “T- part 13x6x1 Lace, Giving You the Ability to Have a Longer or Multi-direction Partings and Makes You More Natural.” If you know what 13x6x1 lace means, then you already knew when you purchased it that the parting space is only 1” wide. But, some people might not know what that 1 means at the end. They might see it, but then see the product page says “ability to have a longer or multi-direction partings” and think they can change the part if they want. Like I said earlier, you can NOT change this part! It is only 1” wide and that whole 1” is plucked out making the middle part. There’s no room to change it. It’s unfortunate because, like I said earlier, you can see the tracks next to the part and if you could change the part you’d have the possibility of covering them up. But, you can’t with this.

Oh, and there’s weird stains inside the cap. They look to be from the combs.

I thought it was really funny in the middle of the product page they had a little thing that said, “Are you satisfied with the 613 blonde lace front wig human hair you bought before? If not satisfied, you can try ours. Maybe we will become the terminator of your choice of blonde lace front wig human hair, and we hope to have the opportunity to become your superstar.” Become the terminator of your choice? What the heck does that mean?! 😂 They definitely are NOT going to become my superstar, or anyone else’s if they keep putting out wigs like this! Especially given the fact they’re charging $102.39 for the 18” body wave (at the time of writing this review) is crazy! It is nowhere near worth that! I definitely do NOT recommend!

This is a lightweight ionic dryer similar to Dyson but much less expensive. It has a digital display of temperature and fan speed. Once you figure out how it works, it is not complicated but I would not use this for guests as they would never figure it out. It has 3 buttons. Middle button is power and toggle. You long press for 2 seconds to turn dryer on/off. You tap button to toggle between controlling fan speed to temp and back. The other two buttons are to increase/decrease the selected item (fan speed or temp).

The digital display tells you the temp setting or fan velocity setting. It displays a red ring when you have it turned to be hot and a blue ring when turned to cold. This is a super high tech good looking device.

My main concern is the highest setting isn't very hot. It gets my short hair dry but takes much longer than other dryers. This makes it unusable.

Temp supposedly adjust between 50 degrees and 99 degrees. This is Celsius so 99 should be over 200 degrees Fahrenheit. It is definitely not that hot.

Fan speed (aka air volume) can be adjusted from 50% of max to 99% of max.

I know that in order to make natural bee wax white some type of bleaching process has to happen so whatever this company uses does something to the wax and omits this terrible metallic smell. Update:
My wife decided to use this Glacier Floss Dental Magnetic Oral Irrigator MADE IN USA. She turned the lever that sent the water to the irrigator with the faucet full on. The tube was forced out inside the handle due to the pressure and large volume of water. It would have lasted years if I had shown her how to use it correctly.
This review isn't really for the Glacier Floss but for the item that replaced it. When I looked through my past purchases I found the Glacial Floss and purchased it again. I was thrilled to find that it was much less expensive.
It arrived today and it's a little hand-held irrigator that you pump with your thumb. I will return it, even if I find it works well. I was deceived and you will be deceived if you read my review from 2014. If you find the Glacial Floss irrigator for sale it is worth the price. It is not this product. Amazon how do you allow this?

I was diagnosed with periodontal disease several years ago. Surgery was recommended as well as the use of an oral irrigator. I purchased the Glacier Floss - no resevoir to fill or clean, no electricity needed. It has worked well, it has kept the surgery at bay and I haven't had a cavity since installing this. I use it every night.

A month ago the kids tried to fill a water balloon with it and it began leaking, no pressure at the tip and water leaking from the seams of the handle. I purchased another and installed it.

I decided to dissect the old one and found that the coiled tube runs continuously from the faucet adapter to the tip of the handle. The coil passes through a series of magnets inside the handle, but I don't believe these magnets have any influence on the effectiveness of this irrigator. The weight does make the handle more substantial, though, and keeps it upright on the side of the sink. Once inside the handle I could see that the only problem was that the tube had slipped of the nipple at the tip of the handle. I will carefully glue the tube back in place and put this in the children's bathroom. I plan to get several more years out of both the new G. F. and the old one, once I have made the repair.

I see that some others have had a similar leaking problem with the Glacier Floss. I recommend that you slow the water coming from the faucet to a light trickle then adjust the flow at the faucet adapter allowing some water to continue flowing from the faucet. The tip allows only a very small stream of water, but at substantial pressure. I believe this stream of water could pierce skin if set too high. excessive pressure from an attempt to increase water flow can also cause the tube to separate from the tip on the inside.

To install, you will need basic mechanical skills, a faucet with a removable areator and a pair of pliers, but installation should take about 10 minutes. I didn't use teflon tape and there are no leaks.

I recommend that everyone use an oral irrigator, and the Glacier Floss has served me well. I also highly recommend the Sonicare toothbrush. These tools will reduce dentist bills and can freshen breath more than you will expect. My wife agrees.

Most of the products that I receive through the Amazon Vine program are decent to excellent, but I sometimes get really bad ones. I never let the fact that I receive the products free affect my ratings. I always call the shots as I see them. This SUPRENT razor is the latest example; its stunning manifestation of idiotic product design catapulted it in one fell swoop to the top of my ignominious list of “Worst Products E-V-E-R!”

It’s so bad that I shan’t waste time enumerating its faults in detail, or in trying to be humorous or clever as I usually do in my reviews. This stinker doesn’t even warrant the effort it takes to make a bulletized list, but herewith I reluctantly give it that much attention:

- It’s too heavy to maneuver around the face or wherever.
- The head is too big for precise shaving in tight areas such as under the nose.
- The “38.5° Golden Shaving Angle” is the wrong angle for just about every surface.
- The worst of its many bone-headed “features” is that the chrome-plated zinc handle is too thin for a firm grip; it slips, slides and spins with Teflon-like frictionlessness in the hand, which is not only annoying but actually dangerous. How could it not occur to the geniuses who designed it that a mirror-smooth chromed metal surface with absolutely NO knurling, stippling or any other texture would be even MORE slippery when held in a wet hand with soapy shaving cream on it? Did anyone even try it out on a real face before they shipped it out the door?
- Speaking of shaving cream, the little can that comes in this set is useless. It’s as light and insubstantial as NASA Aerogel, and disappears to a thin oily layer when rubbed in. I don’t know what it is, but it’s NOT like any other shaving cream that I’ve ever used.
- The huge, unwieldy, six-blade head does NOT glide smoothly across the skin; the blades catch and grab at every opportunity, and do NOT shave closely.
- Since no blade replacements show up on Amazon, they’re clearly rare, hard to find and, if you can find them, no doubt they’re obscenely expensive.
- The stylish, oh-so-elegant “portfolio” that accompanies this set is the most pretentious thing that I’ve seen in a long time. I mean, it’s a RAZOR, not the latest iPad Pro!

Anyone who spends 50 bucks for this set rather than getting it for free will surely be wildly disappointed and probably furious once they realize what they got for their money. It’s not worth 50 cents. It’s all about form over function, with form checking in at 100% and function zero.

In the past, I’ve gotten some marginal razors through Vine, but none have been so bad that I’ve thrown them away rather than using them. This one is the exception.

The minimum-allowed one-star rating is far too generous for this “object” that, whatever it is, doesn’t qualify as a “razor” in any practical way. Caveat emptor!

I have a lot of experience with hair extensions. Both Nano bead, and keratin tip extensions. These were by far THE WORST HAIR EXTENSIONS IVE EVER WORN! Right away I could tell the quality was off, in fact I kept wondering if they were actually synthetic. I even found several that were weighted with thick black threads that were mixed in with the “hair” and firmly glued in with the keratin. I tested their durability with heat styling which they seemed to hold up to, and against my better judgement installed 200 extensions over a period of 2 days. They were problematic from the start, tangled VERY easily, and with very thin ends. Then, about 2 weeks ago I began to notice an odd residue throughout my hair. Fast forward to yesterday morning, and after combing the tangles out of my hair with the dry extensions, I took a shower and used the same paraben free cowash “nopoo” I always use. As I wrapped my hair in my tshirt hair towel I noticed some larger than usual knots. Upon investigating these more closely, I realized that my hair had somehow become one nearly solid mass with a couple of strangely hard softball sized masses in the back and on the side. They had thumb-thick loops of hair that came from various places on my head that seemed to grow out of my head and back into my head, as there were no ends to be found that connected them to various other larger knots and each other. At first I was just kind of bemused, but 13 hours of painful picking through impossibly tight enormous knots that culminated at a single matted extension at the core , who’s binding keratin was degraded to an odd residue, pulling out many other decaying hair extensions and quite a bit of my own hair, amusement was not the emotion I was feeling. Now I’m left with patchy extensions that are still trying to tangle up despite the detangler saturating them and a ravaged scalp. This was the third time i had washed them. My natural hair is in the beginning of its recovery from the treatment required for an illness, and because of that same illness I have been in quarantine since March and unable to work and have very limited funds to spend on another set of full head hair extensions. Which is not ideal.
Take my word for it, there are so many other brands of human hair nano bead extensions that cost around the same to be found on Amazon that there is absolutely no benefit to be had in choosing these.

These beads/beans, in a smaller cup, took over 90 minute to melt. And, the warmer was on 180°(F).

I tried a small amount on my arm. The wax was sticky, not liquidy, and it cooled almost as soon as it hit my skin.

I let it sit there for a few minutes (over 5), and peeled the max off. It didn’t hurt, sting, or cause redness – then again …

THE HAIR WAS STILL THERE

Okay, so my hair on my arm is a little thin. But, if this removes thick hair, shouldn’t it remove thinner hair?

I found another patch, got some warm wax – tried it again. Nope. Tried legs, arms, and under my chin. Nothing. Then again, I see I'm not the only one experiencing issues with these beads/beans.

I may have gotten a bad batch. But, I definitely wouldn’t get these again.

I bought the Alkatraveler stick when my home water ionizer went on the fritz and had to send it to Chanson for repair. I was planning a short trip as well, so I thought this would be a great opportunity to try out the travel ionizer.

I like the size of the device. It's very small, light and easy to transport. You simply drop it in a filtered water bottle or glass and allow it to alkanize the water (15 min or so). Supposedly it raises the pH level by 2 points, but I have not tested this yet. The stick comes with a cheap piece of plastic tubing for storage. I opted to use a paper towel and zip lock bag. I shake out the ionizer and wrap it in the paper towel to absorb any excess water.

The main reason I gave this product only 3 starts is that it is difficult to retrieve from the water. You have to use an implement, like a spoon or tongs to get it out, or else you have to stick your fingers in the glass to get it. You want to submerge the stick so that requires at least 8 oz of water. While traveling, I used a wide mouth plastic bottle to ionize the water, and then poured it into another bottle to drink. It would have been much easier if the device had a chain like a tea infuser ball or something to help remove the stick from the water. I sent feedback to the company and received this reply: "We see your point, and will forward your recommendation. The way the Alka Traveler stick is designed now will not allow a chain to fit in the bottle cap carry case. Thank you for your suggestion."

So, although I was glad to have the device, it is not as convenient as it could be.

8/10/13 Update: I've been using this alkaline stick for almost a month now and I am pretty disappointed with it. I had to resort to keeping the stick immersed in water while I drank since there was no easy way to get it out of the container. Also, I started testing the water for alkalinity. The product description claims the stick raises the water alkalinity by 2 points. I tested my filtered water first, which resulted in 7.0 every time. During three separate tests I left the stick in for 10 min, then 15 min, then 20 min. Every time the water tested at barely 8.0. It never reached 9.0 as I expected. So this product barely raises the alkalinity level. Big waste of money on my part.

I trim my beard quite a bit because I don't want a full bushy backwoods beard so there are always little hairs EVERYWHERE!  This looked like a great solution and I wasn't keen on having suction cups on the mirror necessary for the other style of beard trimming catchalls.  Unfortunately I now know what my cat felt like with that damnable Cone of Shame after he was neutered-I mean seriously no wonder our pets hate those things.  Ultimately if you can figure out how to properly maneuver yourself into position it does do what it says, it catches the little hairs; however there are so many things wrong.  First the wires are too stiff and you end up shaving blind because you cannot see over it without holding the front 'bib' down, this means you are now relegated to shaving with one hand and that is not always possible (or you could try what my ex suggested and use a string, bungee cord or piece of rope to hold it down by tying it to a cabinet knob).  I'm not sure how big some of the people reviewing this item's heads are, but unfastening both the horizontal and vertical Velcro to get it on was fine, but removing it without getting the hair you caught everywhere including sprinkled in the hair on top of your head (that had never happened before..) was a bit of an undertaking--I solved it by only removing it in the shower thus containing the hairs in there and not all over the bathroom floor, counters and the sink.  I didn't have any trouble folding it back into the bag for storage, but I do find it very impractical for the purpose I bought it for.  I wouldn't recommend it unless you have extra long arms (if you can touch the floor while standing and not bending over) and/or your eyes are on the end of long stalks growing form the top of your head (think about a snail's eyes).  If I could send it back I would, but instead I'll just put it in the guest bathroom and suggest it for overnight guests to try out and stand back and laugh.  I'll try one of the mirror mounted suction cup catchalls next time, I now understand why they decided on suction cups...

I was really excited about getting this hair dye and using it but sadly it was a GIGANTIC disappointment 😭

1.) On the bottle, in the item description, etc it says that the color lasts for 45 washes but I can promise you that it does NOT last that long heck it barely even lasted 10% as long as it claims to (and yes that's even with me only washing my hair in cold water, only washing my hair once a week, using color protecting products, etc). Within only 4 washes the color has drastically faded and there's even some spots where the color has completely washed out already leaving bleach blonde patches. There's a few semi/demi hair dyes i've used that will still stay pretty even when fading but unfortunately this isn't one of them- it's not ugly per say but it's really bland, lifeless and has me wanting to rush to the store to buy some more hair dye so I can fix it ASAP. I never thought in a million years i'd ever find a semi/demi hair dye that was worse then Splat when it came to fading but man this dye takes the cake- with me taking care of my colored hair properly Splat will last me 10 washes before it gets to the "ew ugly it faded I need to do a touch up" stage whereas once again this only lasted 4 washes.

2.) This color isn't teal in fact it's more of a dark blue with teal highlights/shine that you can only see if you're outside or standing directly under a light inside. I bleached my hair beforehand getting it 100% bleach blonde because I wanted it to be as bright as possible and even with that it still came out dark (and even while fading it looks blue have yet to see any green). I can't speak for anyone else but a genuine teal color is the unicorn of hair dye in my world- i've been dying and cutting my own hair pretty much only using semi/demi hair dye for over 10 years now and in all that time I have yet to find a genuine teal color. I've pretty much tried every brand I could get my hands on with zero luck- it's either dark blue with teal highlights/shine like this one, 98% green with 2% blue, green, dark green, blue, etc. I know going to a salon is an option and is probably my best bet to get genuine teal but because of my failings for the last decade i'm terrified of spending a couple hundred dollars just to end up with a non teal color again 😣. What in the world is going on? 🤣 It's not the olden days where getting colors is impossible and we had to make our own colors using rare to find items it's 2022 so surely there's a way to get a GENUINE TEAL hair dye!

3.) I can't speak for anyone else but in my experience this is hands down the thickest hair dye i've ever come across. This wouldn't of been an issue for me had the bottle design been the same as a lot of other semi/demi hair dyes are (a short easily accessible resealable cylinder) but since it wasn't and instead was put into a thick, dark and non flexible bottle it was next to impossible to get all the dye out or even see how much was in there. To get it out you either have to mix in some really watery hair conditioner or cut the bottle open and hope you don't hurt yourself or get dye all over the place in the process. While the design is visually really cute it's not practical- you end up wasting a lot of dye because you can't get it all out, in an attempt to get the remaining dye out you have to risk injuring yourself or getting dye all over the place or diluting it, since the bottle is black you have no idea how much dye is in there when you first get it so you won't know if you've been ripped off or not after getting a lot out you'll have no idea how much is still in there, because the dye is so thick and it's badly designed you end up having to constantly hit the bottom of the bottle/squeeze on it really hard/shake it hard etc just to get it out which after 20+ minutes really hurt my hands, you can't use the dye right out of the container like you can with the other cylinder hair dye containers and finally because you can't store any left over dye- the opening is so darn tiny there's no way you'll be able to get this thick dye back inside to use later on.

4.) This cost me $12.99 plus tax per bottle (it took 4 bottles to do my hair because I have really long thick hair) and when I bought it the price didn't bother me in fact it's pretty much average as far as semi/demi hair dye goes (the cheapest hair dye I use costs $10 a piece and the most expensive I use is $15 a piece so this is right in the middle) but after taking into account that it's not a genuine teal color, how insanely quickly it fades, how unpractical the design is, that I can't store unused dye, how much ends up going to waste and all the other negatives the price is definitely not worth it to me.

5.) If you've used semi/demi hair dye as much as I have then you already know about the notorious staining and bleeding that comes with these types of hair dyes haha but FYI this one is worse then what you're used to. With every other semi/demi hair dye i've used by the second wash the bleeding stops, the staining on my skin and ears has gone away, it doesn't stain my skin and ears while wet, scratching my scalp doesn't result in stained fingers and dye under my nails and my fingers won't get stained while I wash my hair but with this dye all those negatives have continued all the way past the 4th wash. Basically this dye has all the negatives of semi/demi hair dye but NONE of the positives 🤷🏻‍♀️

So all in all I really don't like this hair dye and wouldn't recommend it. Tbh the only thing it has going for it is that it does make my hair feel really soft and doesn't leave a weird coating on my hair like some other semi/demi hair dyes do but that doesn't mean much when everything else was a fail. Now that I think about it though I think this dye would be perfect for people who either only want crazy colored hair for a short period of time (like for a halloween costume, cosplay, an event, etc) or for parents whose kid's want to dye their hair a crazy color because it fades really quickly and isn't bright at all and is pretty mellow for semi/demi dye, as for vets like me who actually want long lasting bright color STAY AWAY 🙏🏼😂

I went to the Navy Exchange to buy a new shaving cream brush. They were not selling the individual brushes, but had this brush included in this "bump patrol bonus pack". Second, the bristles fall out on the first shave - getting caught up in the razor and complicating my shave. Third, the bristles are shaped such that you only get about 1/3rd of the bristles of surface contact, unless you REALLY mash this thing into your face (keep in mind, brittle bristles makes this very uncomfortable). By the end of the ordeal even using the bump patrol cream, I think my face is more irritated than it would have been had I never touched the brush in the first place.
If you need to use the treatment, don't buy the bonus pack - the brush is a piece of crap.

I was concerned by the label: "avoid contact with eyes, skin, clothing" and "intended for use as a solvent only". According to WebMD: It's important to note that DMSO is POSSIBLY UNSAFE when applied to the skin. There are reports that industrial-grade DMSO is being used for self-treatment of several disease conditions. Industrial-grade DMSO is not of the same quality as the DMSO that is used for drug research purposes since it may contain impurities. DMSO easily penetrates the skin and brings along impurities and other substances that may be hazardous to health.

DMSO is LIKELY SAFE when used as a prescription medication. Don't use products that are not prescribed by your health professional. There is concern that some non-prescription DMSO products might be “industrial grade”, which is not intended for human use. These products are POSSIBLY UNSAFE, as they can contain impurities that can cause health effects. To make matters worse, DMSO readily penetrates the skin, so it carries these impurities rapidly into the body.
---
Also, therapeutic dosages used are lower than this cream, which is 99% (it might be too high):

"For prevention of some side effects of cancer treatment: 77-90% DMSO is typically applied under medical supervision every 3-8 hours for 10-14 days.
For shingles (herpes zoster): 5-40% idoxuridine in DMSO is within 48 hours after the appearance of a rash and applied every 4 hours for 4 days.
For nerve pain: 50% DMSO solution has been used 4 times daily for up to 3 weeks.
For osteoarthritis: 25% DMSO gel has been used 3 times a day, and 45.5% DMSO topical solution has been used 4 times a day."

I was excited to try this scrub once I started reading some of its many positive reviews. I even signed up for auto-delivery. But then I received my first delivery and tried it. I’m confused about how this has so many positive reviews. This is the worst body scrub I’ve ever tried, by far! I typically love body scrubs whether they’re based w/ sugar, salt, coffee, or just about any exfoliant! I’m not a scrub snob either - I’ve tried tons of different brands and “flavors” and can’t say I have one clear favorite. I’ve used and loved niche natural brands from health food stores, ritzy expensive spa-type brands from dept stores and boutiques, and cheap brands from the drugstore equally. I’ve used scrubs that cost $48 for a smallish tub (yikes!) but had just as excellent results from ones that cost $5 for a huge tub of the stuff. I’ve used brands that rinsed clean and other brands that were so oily I had to use a wooden spoon to stir the separated oils back in to the mixture. I found some quality I liked about every scrub I can remember trying - until this one. This scrub has natural ingredients and I love that! But aside from that I don’t see any real advantages or benefits to this product. I swear my container of this scrub had the oddest consistency I’ve ever encountered! It was like an important ingredient was missing because this was like a tub of flaky, dry salt or sugar. I actually started trying to dig deep into the tub to mix the product, erroneously thinking maybe there was a layer of oil or moisture in the bottom of the container. There wasn’t. It’s just a tub of sandy, dry bits. Period. This product didn’t moisturize at all and it wasn’t even particularly smoothing. I had a hard time patting it on my wet/damp skin, truth be told. Again, I’ve tried scrubs that were on the drier side and enjoyed them. But this was bone dry! I think scrubbing myself with the contents of a sugar bowl would’ve been more effective. This didn’t exfoliate well, had zero moisturizing properties, and had no scent, pleasant or otherwise. It was a disappointing, very odd waste of money and time. I immediately canceled my subscribe and save subscription. Big thanks to Amazon for making THAT part easy, at least. And I’m also very relieved I bought this for what’s listed as the “sale price” as opposed to the laughable, listed suggested retail price. I’ll NEVER buy this again and will avoid the brand as a whole.

Just my .2 cents. I have a Braun model #8985 Series 5. After a year of satisfactory use, I thought I should replace the foil and cutters. I got the one recommended for my shaver, the 51S. I started to use it, and after just a few shaves, I noticed the shaves were not as smooth, and more irritation to my face, than I was getting with my original shaver I had for the past year. Now just after a few shaves, I noticed my cutter was starting to dull. I stuck with it a few more months, and then I started looking for a better cutting block for it. I came on Amazon and read some reviews, and there were many satisfied users of the 30B kit. . I even called Braun, and told them my situation, and asked if I could change over to the 30B, instead of staying with the 51S. NO WAY said the rep, use only the cartridge recommended by Braun, the 51S. Well, I decided otherwise, and went to "Target", and got the 30B replacement foil and cutter. Boy, what a difference. It fits right in, no problem with the foil or the cutter fitting, I even like the foil better than the 51S, seems to roll over my fact smoother. The shaves seem so much better. Now to be honest, I have not used the razor much yet, but I'll get back to you with my thoughts when I do. On my #8985 there is a light that comes on, and it says "change foil", which came on right then when I changed the foil over to the 30B, it lite up. There is a reset button right there, and if you push it with a pen or pencil point, the light goes out after blinking a few times. Maybe the 30B is the way to go, and the 30B is about $15 cheaper than the 51S. I don't know what Braun is doing, but it is not making me buy a new Braun. If I get upset with their shaver, I'm not going to buy a new Braun, I will switch brands. Hate to say this folks, but every manufacturer out there is trying to rip us off today! Regards, TC

My dentist took one look at my inflamed gums, and strongly suggested I start using an electric toothbrush. I knew a cheapie like this wouldn't last, but I got it to tide me over until I got a proper electric brush. Even so, this brush was so disagreeable that it induced me to shell out money sooner than I wanted to get a quality brush.

This comes packed with medium bristles. I was wondering why it was so stiff, but then I went out and got a pack of soft bristles, which barely helped. The problem with this brush is that it rotates so fast that you have to use a lot of pressure to keep the bristles in contact with your teeth, otherwise it just bounces off them when you use light pressure. This makes it really hard to control and achieve any degree of precision. Even with all the extra pressure I exerted, I still had plaque in easy spots that I couldn't reach with this brush.

Don't be pulled in by the price. I consider the thing dangerous; it rotates lightning-fast and requires hard pressure. The whole time I used it, I worried that it was going to damage my gums even more than they were already. After about a week I ordered a Rotadent, and finally learned what all the fuss was about electric toothbrushes. Spending extra on a good electric toothbrush is worth it. Don't waste your time with junk like this.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
First, the good: I enjoy the smell of this product. And I'll probably use the whole stick just because it smells nice, and provides a light tingling sensation. Apart from that, I've noticed no difference in moisture (blackhead reduction, or any of the other laundry list of things it claims to cure).

I got a decent laugh out of my first use, quickly realizing you can't simply roll this onto your face for complete coverage. You have to get this on your fingers to cover the contours of the nose, for example. The description of the product mentions "Blackhead Removal Strips", but those were nowhere to be found in what I received. Once this dries, I simply wash it off of my face, and see/feel exactly what I did when I initially washed my face the first time. Lastly, it's a bit overpriced as far as facial masks go.

So look, I like the soothing sensation of masks as much as the next person. Therefore please understand that I far from hate this product. I simply don't think it's providing much value. Even the satisfaction of a peel-able mask is absent here. But if you really want to pay to smell some tingling green tea drying on your face, then this will get you there. I just wouldn't expect much else from it. The laughably fake "before and after" shots should tell you plenty about the true efficacy of this product.

I have been a long time Norelco shaver user. When it was time to buy a new set of Series 7 Lift-and-Cut heads for my old Norelco 6885XL razor, I decided to get the new 9170XLCC razor. Big Mistake! The new 3-ring Smart Touch heads are not as good as the old reliable Lift-and-Cut heads.

Why you say? To make the head look like it has more surface area and thus should cut faster, the Norelo engineers reduced the cutting area of the fastest, outer, ring, to squeeze in the two inner, but slower surface speed, rings. In fact the outer ring cutting blades are only 1.00 mm wide as opposted the the 1.75 mm width cutter width in the series 7 Lift-and-Cut heads. The added inner rings actually cause pulling of the beard hairs if you try to shave at the same speed you did with the older models.

By the Way, the so-called cleaning system is a big bother and not worth the extra cost. You can rinse the 9170XL under the faucet just like the older XL models. In fact, you HAVE TO rinse it because of the sticky mess the cleaning system leaves in the razor after "cleaning."

The bottom line: In a failed attempt to make a quieter, faster, shaving system, Norelco actually made it WORSE than earlier lift-and-cut models. Then to top that off, changed the drive pin design so that one can NOT use the superior heads. Do not waste your hard-earned cash on this sub-par Norelco product.

$130 for this razor kit is a great buy.

What's in the box:
Stainless Steel 3-piece razor with 3 base plates (6 possible shave settings)
5 Blade Pack - An image on this page says it comes with 20. That's not true. It only comes with 5.
Shaving Cream (4oz)
Synthetic Brush
There is NOT a blade bank included in this box.

Review:
This is my first 'Double Edge' or 'Safety Razor'. I've tried all of the various cartridge razors before this, and I can't believe it's taken me this long to try a safety razor that uses plain steel blades. Update - After trying the plates, I'm really happy with the 2/4 plate for this razor. I can make the 1st pass on 4, then use 2 for the 2nd pass and get a really good BBS shave.

Also, this is my first time trying a shaving brush. This brush is soft, and does an excellent job lathering. I'm using way less of the shaving cream than I expected.

The razor is clearly solid, and is much heavier than the Harry's razor, or any other cartridge I've ever used. The handle is shorter than what I'm used to, at about 3-1/4", but turns out to be just the right length for dealing with the various ways I needed to hold this kind of razor to shave.

The shaving cream that comes with this kit is definitely the right stuff for shaving this way. It lubricates well, lathers well, and smells pretty good.

Since the kit didn't come with a blade bank, I've ordered one (also from amazon - the price here is better than the price on Rockwell's webpage). It should be here before I need to dispose of a used blade.

Overall - Glad I found this kit. It's a keeper.

PS - I'm still keeping my Harry's cartridge razor for travel. I don't like checking a bag for overnight business trips, and you're not allowed to take these razor blades through TSA at the airport.

So after I bought two of these I threw out my one piece clip in extensions made by a different brand, because they're no where near as great as these. I wish I never would've spent the money on those so I could've bought more of these! These were an absolute dream. The first time I tried one on I knew I made the right choice. After heat styling it I was completely sold! I'm a customer for life now! The hair is so soft and so manageable even after curling! Well.... tight curls were a nightmare to try and comb through, I almost gave up and didn't even bother. But those sexy loose natural curls are manageable. They do get a tad bit frizzy but no where near as frizzy as most synthetic hair pieces. So I did buy two because I assumed I would need them both since the comments said they were thin. They aren't as thin as people say but if you layer them like I did, then you'll need two. I did take the wire off one and sewed it to the one I layered. One was definitely not enough. It might've been because I have a bob growing out so I really had to get in these extensions and layer them. Now as far as heat, I didn't go over 300 degrees and I used a good curler from Sally's we used in cosmo. No damage, no melting, no problems. I will say the wet steam styling didn't work, like the synthetic styling they talk about on YouTube where you wet the hair and heat style it on low. Nope didn't work. You can just roll these in a curling iron and then hold the curl in your hand (don't burn yourself the curl is hot af, use a glove or something like pin or rollers) I just don't recommend tight curls unless you have the patience to deal with the frizzy and the tangles. It was an absolute nightmare! Loose curls totally work way better and you can definitely run your fingers through them. Just once again, they won't stay curled unless you hold the curl in your hand or you pin it until they cool off. Also, it's super comfortable to wear, after I layered them and it didn't feel like I was wearing a coat on my head anymore lol i don't know if I'm wearing it in the right spot but the weft kinda hides at the nape of my head, just underneath the curve of my skull. My husband likes to touch the back of my head when he leans down to kiss me (he's tall) and I got my fingers crossed he doesn't feel them this weekend when we go out. They don't stick out and they lay smooth against my head even after I doubled the extensions. These were such a great buy, I wanna buy more ASAP! I did cut a few inches off because they were pretty long before and after curling. I will probably be adding clips to the inside of the extensions just for extra support because it can easily slip off if you're not careful. On the inside there is little clips that attach to the inside of some loops sewn along the seam that help tighten the wire.

This kit is so cool! I’m a huge makeup lover. With that comes sometimes getting palettes I order online that come with broken pans or having palettes I own end up with broken pans. I would always repress them myself, but it always bothered me because they never looked quite the same afterwards. I also like to de-pot singles and put them in magnetic palettes, and it can be complicated and/or I can end up breaking the product. I didn’t even know they made sets like this, but, when I saw this, I needed to try it!

There’s a medium sized magnetic palette in plastic wrapping and then the fix kit in a small box. When you open the box, you’ll take out a plastic box, a small magnetic palette in plastic wrapping, and the makeup repair solution in plastic wrapping. So, you ask, where are the rest of the parts? They fit together in that plastic box! It makes it nice and compact so everything is all together but not taking up a bunch of room. The plastic box, you lift off the main lid, you’ll see a layer that has a strainer type thing in the center and a layer that has 3 circular areas filled with black. You remove the plastic layer with the 3 circular areas, and it reveals 3 black cylinder tower type things. You can lift the layer with the sifter, which will reveal just a bottom plastic part of the plastic box. In the bottom, you’ll find a plastic bag that has the empty tin pans in different sizes - you get 3 sets of 3 sizes. I thought it was nice to get 3 sets of the different sizes. You also get 2 black tools to help put the powder products into the pans or circular areas to flatten them.

Overall, I think this an amazing kit! Is it something anyone who uses makeup needs? No. Especially when everything you can do with this kit, you can DIY without it. But, this kit does make the process easier. So, if you’re a huge makeup lover, order a lot of makeup products online (where you could end up getting broken pans), travel a lot where your products tend to break, just end up with broken products at home, or de-pot products a lot - then I’d say this would be a great kit for you or as a gift for someone who know who fits those things! Again, it’s not something you NEED. But, it’s definitely something that makes things easier!

Brian doesn't care about dual forms, but I do! Hi! I'm Drea, Brian's wife and I purchased these forms. :o) First let me be very clear here: THEY ARE NOT REGULAR NAIL TIPS! These are forms that give 2 uses hence the word DUAL (which means 2) These forms are for use with a product called POLYGEL. Polygel is a perfect mix of acrylic and gel products. The beauty of this marriage is that the polygel is cured in an UV/LED light. The function of the dual form, is to hold the amount of polygel you need to achieve a completely covered nail in one go. You fill the dual form with polygel, use 91% alcohol as a slip solution and pat, pat, pat that polygel until it is where you want it. You then turn the filled form over and apply from the cuticle to the nail's free edge. You do clean up with the alcohol around the form's edges because there will be gel coming out of the sides, and then cure under the UV/LED lamp for 30 to 60 seconds WITH THE DUAL FORM STILL ON. This 100 pcs set is perfect for achieving the above goal. What I can say about them is that I got two sizes and that is fine with me. I am grateful for the two sizes as I have narrow shaped nails and a slender nail bed. I can only review the sizes right now as I am waiting for my polygel order. Once I receive that order then I can review the form properly. I can also say that it is awesome that they come with the length box that allows you to see how far you are "moving" the polygel up in the form. I know they will work for me.

This product contains nine packets with different respective extracts, to create jelly face masks. The nine varieties include the following highlight ingredients: Grape Seed Extract, Lemon Extract, Camellia Tea Extract, Passion Fruit, Strawberry Extract, Gold Foil, Cocoa Fruit Powder, Pistachio Seed Oil and Blueberry Extract.
The instructions are fairly simple and easy to follow. Open a packet and mix with 30ml of water into a bowl. Apply liberally onto the face and neck. Allow to dry, then peel the mask away from the face and neck.
The packets hold a considerable amount of powder. If used only on the face, there’s enough product for two faces. So, you could share or save for another treatment.
The significant other opted to test the Lemon Extract Jelly Mask. We both felt it has a nice, mild scent. She used half of the packet, and mixed it with water. She had enough for good coverage with reasonable thickness. After it dried/set, she eventually peeled it off. It came off in a few pieces. She said it did make her skin feel tighter and refreshed. So, we both agreed it met the descriptions in the product details.
This statement from the product details caught her attention: “Face jelly mask powder is made of organic plant and fruit material and is vegan. Suitable for all skin types including dry, oily and sensitive skin.” She’s thrilled with it being vegan, and the use of organic components.
So, the jelly face mask powder does deliver on intended use (at least the tested Lemon variety). She gives it a thumbs up, so it receives a 4.5 star rating.

I just finished nursing my child and wanted to take care of myself starting with skincare. I had acnes back in highschool. I tried multiple laser treatments and it did very little to clear up my acnes scars. Plus one laser treatment cost atleast $500 and they quoted that I would need about 10 sessions to clear up my skin. That would be $5,000! So I did 3 laser sessions which had very little result and tried to do home treatment such as salicylic peel, retin a and dermaroller.
I strongly advise not to use salicylic or other peels at home as I burnt my skin and have permanent scar from it.

Retin a is good that it brighten up my skin but did little for my acnes scar or shrink pores. I tried dermaroller with vitamin c & hyaluronic serum but it really did nothing for my skin.

I read a skincare article that human stem cell containing EFG could reduce pore size & acnes scars. As I have tried many methods before, I was hesitant to purchase another item but just gave it another last try.
I searched and found Anterogen human stem cell skin pack. I read all the reviews and googled more information about stem cell skincare. There are two stem cell that is in the market. One is plant based( apple stem cell) vs human stem cell. You can google this yourself but all the articles state that plant based stem cell does nothing for your skin. It has to be human stem cell! So I purchased this brand as it had the highest amount of human stem cell.

I sanitized my dermaroller (1mm) in boiling hot water for 5 mins. I washed & dry my face then apply Anterogen white silk timeless machine serum on my skin. Then roll dermaroller roller over my face applying more serum on punched skin. Then finished it with this human stem cell mask. I left it on my skin for 30 mins. I also squeezed left over serum from mask on a facial bowl and tapped it on my skin and left.

The next morning, omg my pores &acnes scar finally looked smaller!! I literally teared up as I have found something that could help my skin look better. I am planning to do dermaroller every 2 weeks using Anterogen human stem cell serum with mask. Remember, don't over do it as skin needs downtime to recover and produce new collagen to fill up pores, scars or wrinkles.

I was sent this brush free of cost to review. I used it a few times and was pretty satisfied with it. Here is what I think of it:
Pros:
1. It is extremely easy to use, even on dry hair. Just part the hair into sections and run the comb through each section.
2. The straightener comes with adjustable temperature and a simple way to switch from celsius to Fahrenheit. The range specified is 170 C- 200 C for thin hair, 190-210 for medium and between 210 and 230 for thick hair. I used the brush at 220 and it worked well for me.
3. The brush heats up pretty quickly and it displays the temperature while heating.
4. The straightening brush can be used to give the hair a natural look by combing once and an iron straight look by using it over and over again.
Cons:
1. I found it a little difficult to straighten my thick hair, especially on the scalp as the brush cannot penetrate through my thick hair. When I divided it into multiple parts, it was easier to straighten, but took way too long compared to a straightening iron.
2. The brush is tad too heavy to brush through my thick hair!

Overall, it is a wonderful tool to get natural looking straight hair or even to touch up straightened hair. I loved the product!

I own a hair salon and highly recommend these lashes to all my clients. I apply them to most clients. Maybe my little tricks might help you. I highly recommend this product.

For myself personally, I like to cut my lashes in half for daytime makeup. Cutting these lashes is fine because there are plenty of magnets.

Ladies, lashes are not 1 size fits all so gently and Modestly trim the inside edge(side closest to your nose) of your eyelash to fit to a size best for you.

The magnets stay firmly for DAYS if you use my method. KEY: you will ALSO need DUO eyelash adhesive AND a fine line sable paint brush from an art/craft store and your mascara. THE LASHES WILL STAY FOR DAYS IF YOU PREFER. Or I like to use olive oil to remove.

NOTE: mascara - liquid adhesives - eyeliner need 30 seconds to set both on your eyes and on the lashes BEFORE you bond the two together

1. Apply your own mascara to your eyelashes - I prefer monsieur big by Lancôme.
2. Trim the eyelash to the size you desire (I normally cut mine in half).
3. Apply the magnetic eyeliner with a fine line sable art brush from an art store.
4. Dab a little of the eyeliner on each magnet on the lash itself.
* I ALSO USE DUO EYELASH ADHESIVE AND LINE EYES WITH A FINE LINE OF THIS ADHESIVE YO MY EYES AS WELL AS THE LASH MAGNETS
6. Close your eye. Stick the lash in place.
7. Open your eye and Quickly make any adjustments and move the lash if necessary.
7. Clean away any smudging.
8. Smile because you’re super gorgeous! Air kisses to yourself in the mirror!

I was shopping for replacement cutters and combs for a Norelco Micro Action (formerly Lift & Cut [formerly Rotatract]) shaver and noticed that for less than $10 more I could have a whole new Norelco shaver. I was sold.

Norelco Reflex Plus shavers combine 4 features pioneered by Norelco and improved over time. Rotary heads reduce the vibration common to reciprocating shavers. Floating heads individually hug the skin. Lift and Cut blades gently pull whiskers into the cutter for a closer shave. Everything rides on a set of pivoting platforms that bulge slightly at the center of the head assembly. The bulge allows the heads to maintain contact with the contours of difficult to shave spots like the concave hollows of the neck below the chin.

I've been a Norelco man from my first crop of peachfuzz to my current orchard of gray quills, so the first shave wasn't a surprise for my skin. It was as close and comfy as I'd expect from a Norelco.

The real revelation was the sound. The previous Lift and Cut was like shaving with a Black & Decker DustBuster. The Reflex Plus is so quiet, you can actually hear the cutters slice off the whiskers and then fall silent on the next pass over the same area. This is a real help for those times when a mirror isn't nearby. You could actually shave by the sound alone!

A somewhat poignant note: Models at the economy end of the Norelco line are now made in China and lack carrying bags of any kind. When I travel, I roll my shaver in an article of clothing, usually a T-shirt, so the carrying case is no biggie. Still, I miss seeing the words "MADE IN HOLLAND" on the bottom of every Norelco I've owned.

Times may change but at least the quality of the shave has only improved.

For this price you get 6 individually sealed containers of remover pads. They each contain 38 thin fabric-like removal pads that are soaked in the non-acetone remover. The containers screw open and don't seem to dry out easily. The remover contains isopropyl myristate, propylene carbonate, fragrance, and water. These are ideal for anyone who doesn't like the smell of acetone since they just smell flowery. They smell wonderful, I'm someone who doesn't like many scented things, but they are all very soft pretty scents that I love.

The pads remove polish more slowly than most acetone-based nail polish removers and require a bit of scrubbing. To remove a bright red (read-as nail polish that stains) manicure I use 3-4 sheets (more if there is glitter in the polish). They do leave your nails and hands a bit greasy feeling (which means they moisturize your nails rather than drying them out like acetone) so you should always wash your hands thoroughly after using the remover pads. Overall, great product and I will buy it again (once these run out, they last forever!)

I've been using the Diffuser for a few weeks and I found it to be a great unit. I like that you do not need distilled water to use it. Its the first we've owned that doesn't need distilled water.

The directions state to use only 3 to 5 drops of oil. I found that using 3 drops doesn't do much. Depending what oils I'm adding to the diffuser I can easily drop 5 to 8 drops. For the most part, 5 drops is what we are happy with. It will keep a 200 square foot room diffused with oils as long as the diffuser is running.

The lighting effects work great and we generally run them at night as a night light in the kitchen. At other times we run it for fun. The timers works great but we rarely use that feature. We just turn it on and it runs for several hours (never timed it) until it runs out and shuts off.

I don't like the ending noise alerts. They are loud and at night they will wake us up. I can't complain to much about this because most diffusers have the loud beeping noise.

Tips:

Before adding more drops then the instructions states, follow their suggest usage and see if you like the smell. If its not enough, then add more drops until you get the desired effect during your next few runs.

Don't set it up to close to you or your work space. If its set it up to close, I found that the mist creates is very strong and gives me a headache. For the most part, I only use it when I'm working on the other side of the room. When I need to be near the diffuser, I turn off until I'm done.

My hair was falling out badly. Over 4 years, I could not figure out why more was in my drain or brush than on my head. The VA didnt know why (I am retired military), and to be honest, they really weren't interested in finding the answer or solution. I am a curly girl with mixed-race hair; its not that thick (anymore) but my hairs porosity is - well - it dries fast but loses moisture fast as well. (High porosity I think.) I look for products which are free of unfriendly curly girl ingredients, and use henna on my head for reducing the curls tightness; opting for the conditioning value of henna rather than the damaging ingredients of OTC hair dye and heating tools. I hopped online and began journey into the ethers of the rabbit hole (internet) and began the exhaustive journey on which oils - specifically essential oils and Ayurvedic - for my conundrum, which is hair loss and thinning. LOTS of products and I wanted to try them ALL. I was SO overwhelmed, has 40 items in my cart (you know exactly what I am talking about), and angry that I would have to wait on ANYTHING I wanted to try. I was just about ready to delete everything in my cart, when I saw this bottle show up on my screen. It was aluminum and I thought well, it cant hurt to look. The ingredients are not scientifically multisyllabic; pretty simple and straight forward. I figured, "Well I cant sped $$$+ or $. So I bought this (in 2018) and figured I had nothing to lose except more hair. (Oh great...)

The product smell amazing to me. However it will be strong to others. If you are offended by, herbally, natural, woodsy, earthy, along the lines of patchouli smell, dont buy it. There is no need to bash how you dont like the smell. However, if you are a fan of the smell, like me, you will be fine. There is sediment because of the herbs in the oil, so it will need to be shaken before applied. Anyway, when I started I would put it on my head before washing my hair; usually an hour or so and just let it hang out. (Didnt know what to expect.) I cowashed my hair, conditioned and styled my hair; always air drying. Then SPARINGLY - and I do mean that, I would put a little on my scalp mid week. I forgot about looking for any results because I was so dismayed at what was happening. After a month or so it dawned on me, I wasnt seeing any hair in the shower. I also noticed the density looked fuller. At work I received comments and loved the results. I am a little vain when it comes to my hair. Live was good, and my hair was returning to normal. Fast forward...

After a year, my hair was gorgeous - THEN COVID. Finances ran lean and cuts needed to be made. I have not used this in almost a year and my hair is horrible. JUST HORRIBLE... thinning, no density, still curly but not bouncey and full. I could no longer spare the expense; I am buying two bottles - I can NOT be without this product. It really REALLY works. I have been using electric toothbrushes for years, so this review is comparing this electric toothbrush to the others I've used.

The thing I love most about this toothbrush is no splatter! I love how clean electric toothbrushes get my teeth, but they all splatter somewhat when you have to spit, and the last one I bought was the worst. My bathroom mirror looked dirtier than the kids' most of the time. But I have no issues with this toothbrush. The base with holder is larger than what I like, but the holder is easily removable to make the base smaller, not much bigger than the toothbrush base. This toothbrush is lighter and slimmer than my other electric toothbrushes. It charges for a long time. I took it on a 9 day trip and it stayed charged the whole time. According to the manual a full charge will last for 90 minutes, so two minutes a day, twice a day would be a whopping 22 days of usage before needing a recharge. It also seems to get my teeth even a little bit cleaner than my other electric toothbrushes. I'm about due for my next dentist's appointment, but after using this toothbrush my teeth almost have that just-polished feeling to them. I do not press hard at all, just let the toothbrush do its work as is advised with all electric toothbrushes. As the manual stated I might, I did feel a bit of a tickling sensation the first time or two I used it, but not since. I did not feel any of the weak ionic electric current in my hand, as the manual also stated is possible for some users.

The one thing I do not like is the timer mechanism. It doesn't show you the actual time brushed, just signals once every thirty seconds then twice every two minutes. A lot of times I am not paying that close of attention. With my old toothbrush I could just take a quick look at the timer to see the actual time, but with this one there is no way to know if I've gone over time or not long enough until I go another full two minutes. I wish at least it would buzz twice every thirty seconds once the two minutes has been reached.

Two things I don't like about this toothbrush are no actual timer and no battery indicator.

This review is for the 3 Pack (White/Slate/Lake blue) of the Niutop Watchband Style Band for Fitbit One. I received a promotional discount on this item in exchange for providing a review. I have been using this item daily for a little over a month and wanted to share my experience.

First Impressions
* The items were exactly as pictured, the colors really bright and crisp.
* It took some work getting the FitBit One in and out of the band. It gets a little easier the more you use it. I do not view this as a problem as I know its not going to fall out.
* Was not easy to insert the fasteners on the one end of the band to the connectors on the other. This is still and issue, but again, I do not view this as a negative as I can trust that it will remain secure, but it can be a pain, easier with help, to fasten it.

Observations from wearing.
* The FitBit One was very secure in the band, never worried nor experienced it falling out, coming loose, etc.
* Once fastened securely the band never unsnapped by accident.
* After the first week or so I started to get a rash on my wrist. I switched it to the other wrist and experienced the same thing. I took off the band, removed the FitBit, then washed the band in soap and water. I wore it for several weeks after this, on the same wrist, and did not experience any issues.
* I was used to clipping my FitBit to my pocket or shirt, and do not normally wear a watch. I did not have any problem wearing it, was very comfortable and often forgot I even had it on. It did take some getting used to, remember to remove for a shower, and not getting it overly wet while washing my hands, but I got used to it very quickly.
* I did notice a few occasions that if I made exaggerated arm movements it would trigger as steps on my FitBit one.

Overall
I would recommend this for anyone looking for a watchband style carry for their FitBit. I use mine daily and I not even considered going back to clip style carry. I do recommend that when you first receive it that you wash it with soap and water, rinse and let dry before using. You will never need to worry about the FitBit becoming unsecured from the band.

I am going to be straight up with you all. When I found out I was receiving these products to review I was sort of nervous. For one thing I have not used an eyelash curler since I was a teen. Second of all, I was really not sure at all about the hair remover. It looked like something that would be used in torture. Now that I have used them, (after my daughter took the initial test run and she turned out okay) I love them!

First of all they are pretty tools in pretty boxes! They are so girly and pretty and pink, and red, and I love that! I thought that being pink that my husband would leave them be as he is always using my tools, but nope, he got a splinter woodworking tonight and came out after getting it out of his skin and asked where the pink tweezers came from. I gave him the run down about it and he said they were a lot better than our other tweezers, which for the record were pretty good too!

Now I will say, the hair remover can be a bit painful but no more painful than trying to tweeze those delicate areas. It does the job a lot faster too. I have fair skin and light facial hair so unless in the sun you can barely see it but in the sun I look a bit furry, even at my lip line. I have used the hair remover on my upper lip and corners of my mouth and while it didn't feel great, it was not too bad and now I have a smooth lip! I also did my hairline and face. It works after you get the hang of it which didn't take long to do.

I was surprised with the lash curler. I remember the curlers from my youth, always sticking on my lashes, pulling them out, but I also do not remember them having the nice slick black stuff on them. I guess we have come a long way in non stick surfaces! I also learned my lashes are naturally longer on my right eye than my left. Interesting, never noticed that before. I can now have lovely curly lashes before applying mascara!

Lastly, the tweezers ... nothing can compare to a great tweezer! I hate when the ends do not come together completely, useless. These tweezers are perfect and really get the job done.

I like having my "girly" tools now, they are pretty to use, and I know it seems shallow, but when I have to pluck, tweeze, and remove hair from my face, I prefer to do it with something pretty rather than utilitarian!

And yes for the record I did get this free but I would never review something I do not personally enjoy using.

I received this product heavily discounted. For ladies or gentlemen  who are unfamiliar with how Retinol works, let me explain. Retinoids work by prompting surface skin cells to turn over and die rapidly, making way for new cell growth underneath. They hamper the breakdown of collagen and thicken the deeper layer of skin where wrinkles get their start. There is a myth that it thins the skin and this is simply not true. This is the second 7775X I have owned. The first lasted two years, but this after extensive travel all over the world. It does shave as well as a blade (I use one of those too now and then) if you use it right (see below)

Positives

1) Quick charging - less than an hour to charge.
2) Long lasting - I have used it 10 days without recharging - great if you travel.
3) Seems to prevent ingrown hairs - which is something I run into when I use a blade consistently. My face definitely breaks out much less when I use this razor versus a blade (and I own some expensive blade razors as backup!).
4) So long as you follow instructions (don't press down hard, but when you need to go over an area again, do it firmly) you won't get nicked. Nice when you are in a strange hotel in a strange time zone and waking up jet lagged but needing to look presentable for a meeting.

Negatives

1) A little expensive
2) The shaving lotion cartridges are also expensive - I would just buy a can of regular shaving Gel (eg Edge).
3) Constantly pressing the dispenser for more gel can be a pain in the neck, and you go through those cartridges quickly (one every 10 days at most). If I wanted to redesign this shaver, I would junk the shaving dispensor entirely - I now find it just another moving part with the hinged lid.
4) I wish Norelco had come up with a way for this razor to use a standard charger jack of some kind, as having another electrical cord when I travel (especially one that does not work with multiple corded adaptors such as I-go) means I don't take the cord unless I am gone more than 8-10 days.

To use this right, just buy regular shaving gel, put it on your face, wait 30 seconds for the gel to soften your beard, and go for it. This is the best way I have found to get a clean, smooth shave. Gel in a can also has the advantage of going on thickly (versus the Coolskin dispensor) and not drying up quickly. Also, having a can of the shaving gel when you travel (checked baggage of course) can also come in handy if your Norelco runs out of charge, and you need to switch to that backup Gillette you should have in your shaving kit (I travel with enough cords as it is).

I bought this to begin (and win!) the fight against the wrinkles that are appearing around my eyes (crow's feet). I guess the best solution is not to laugh, but then what fun would life be...

What is Hyaluronic acid? According to WebMD, "Hyaluronic acid works by acting as a cushion and lubricant in the joints and other tissues. In addition, it might affect the way the body responds to injury."

(+) Does it work? I've used the Hyaluronic serum every night for a week now. Not sure if I can say 100% that I have noticed no fine lines around my eyes, but I've had 2 friends remark that my skin is looking great. As we women know, that's a good endorsement right there.

(+) Texture: As you can see in the photo, the Derma-nu serum is a clear, slightly viscous consistency that goes on clear. You can feel it on your skin for quite a few minutes afterwards. It does NOT leave your skin feeling greasy (big pet peeve of mine) when you wake up in the morning.

(+) Smell: This is not a scented beauty product. There is a very slight almost medicinal scent - that's the best way to describe it. It is not unpleasant, it is extremely mild, but it smells like it has some ingredients that 'have a purpose', vs. beauty products that have fragrances added.

(+) Packaging and ease of use: The pump is well made - it dispenses a small amount of serum, which I am finding is enough for applying to the corners of both eyes. I'm having to "prime" the pump about 2-3 times before it dispenses the serum, so be careful, you don't want to double pump the serum unless you are OK putting possibly 2x the amount on your face than you might have intended.

(+) A little goes a long way. I travel a lot, so the compact bottle and efficient dispensing from the pump are bonuses for me.

(/) Organic. The bottle indicates that 72% of the ingredients are organic. It doesn't clarify which of the ingredients are/are not organic. It would be nice to see this get to 100%.

Bottom line: So far, my skin has felt good, I've had a few compliments, and I'm pleased with the way Derma-nu packaged the Hyaluronic serum so that it is easy to dispense.

*I received the serum for evaluation and review

I have always been a shaver until I finally got tired of it and decided to try waxing. Contrary to my friends' opinion, I realized waxing was not that painful. (I have had 2 kids naturally...now nothing else can't even hold a candle to that kind of pain!) I actually enjoyed the long gaps I could go between wax jobs. But then as I got more comfortable with waxing, I started wondering how there couldnt be a less messier way to get rid of body hair. And thats when I saw an epilator listing on amazon, appearing in related products. I went through almost all of the zillion reviews listed and that itself is a great tutorial if you want to get a product. In almost a couple days, I had compared, studied and made up my mind too! I finally bought Braun Silk Epil Female Epilator SE7921 and I can honestly say, that this is what I have been looking for.
Now about the product:
Cons: It hurts, but more like a small electric current over your skin. I get angry red bumps, (which happened when I used to wax too) but I have sensitive skin and I am ok with it. It goes away in about 90 minutes and I apply Eucerin Calming lotion after I use Epilator. If you are prone to ingrown hair like me, then make sure you use a good exfoliating scrub/loofah/ the exfoliation system that comes with this pack once a week.
I have even tried using it on my underarms (it definitely hurts more than the small electric current, and I have to use it in a gentle tapping motion rather than the sweep I do in my arms and legs)
Pros: My skin is smoother because I exfoliate regularly now. My body hair is finer and takes at least 2 weeks to grow back to noticeable lengths. My underarms are softer and lighter because I have stopped shaving. Even the hair that grows back is less noticeable.
Not to mention my little investment has paid off nicely, now that I dont have to buy wax strips.
Overall, I am a happy customer. But since this product comes not so cheap, my advise would be to try this product once and see how you feel about it, and then buy it.

When I first bought this product, I was worried by other reviews I saw. Difficulty inserting the probe, the probe breaking shortly after purchase, machine not working, etc. But I'm pleased to say none of these things have happened with mine! The device came with a back up probe, but I've had this device for a month and haven't needed to use it! The probe might bend slightly (I actually prefer mine to have a slight angle to it), but this is quickly resolved by gently bending it back in place.

Is it hard to do? Nope! If you're the type of person who regularly plucks hairs in the mirror, using this device is a piece of cake. All it takes is a steady hand, precision, and patience. I treat the hairs I want to remove with a normal, non-magnifying mirror and my phone flashlight.

Does it cause scarring? My first time was a bit rough as I was still getting the hang of correct insertion angles. The result of that session was a couple of larger scabs that eventually healed back to normal. When you insert the probe down the hair shaft, sometimes there will be slight swelling directly around the entry point. The day after treatment, you may see small, pinpoint scabs over some entry points. But that is normal and they go away quickly.

Is it painful? To me, not at all. Some areas of the body are more sensitive than others. But I use this device mainly on my jawline. Compared to electrolysis appointments I've gone to, the sensation is much less painful! All you feel is a tingling, pinching sensation if the probe is inserted correctly.

Overall, purchasing this device instead of spending $200 a month for a 1-hour electrolysis appointment is wayyyy better for my budget and gives the same results.

My dentist recommended the Oral B Vitality and I purchased one in June '08 and have been using it ever since. To be honest I purchased this particular one because it was green (they have a blue version also). This is an inexpensive electic toothbrush that does the job. According to the directions, if it is charged it the first time for ~16 hours it stays charged for 5 days of uses for 2/day at 2 minutes/use (the brush has a built in timer and pulses at 2 min.). I charge mine every few days by leaving it in the charger overnight, but you can leave it in the charger constantly as long as you let the battery run down once every 6 months (extends rechargeable battery life).

The dual clean comes with the larger, "dual clean" brush heads, but the brush is compatible with most of the Oral B brush heads (including the smaller single brush head ones). I used both the dual and the singles and both worked fine, but switching from one to the other takes a couple of days to get used to as you get used to the size difference.

My then 1 year old Lab seemed very interested in the toothbrush while I was brushing... so I swapped out the brush head (the brush head is the only part one's mouth touches) and tried it on his teeth and he was very agreeable to it... so now that he has his own and I brush his 1-2X/wk I'm hoping it will delay a costly dental visit for him. I have heard they can be several hundred $$.

I bought one for my sister this past Christmas (along with extra replacement brush heads) as she was shopping for one and she likes it also... makes a good gift.

I was back at the dentist in Dec. '08 for a check-up and while my teeth are usually pretty clean anyway they were even cleaner... he practically had nothing to do... so I think that speaks for itself.

This sponge dries really fast, so you don't have to worry much about mildew forming on it.
This New Leaf Konjac sponge is 100% natural and I recommend it to anyone with acne or blackheads.
You can either soak the sponge in warm water for about 2 minutes or you can pour warm water directly onto it and knead it until it gets softer.
Then you can apply your facial cleanser directly onto the sponge, and squeeze it a little, gently massage the sponge until it lathers.
Finally, just gently rub the foam onto your face concentrating on those areas that have blackheads.
Once you've finished cleansing, rinse the sponge with warm water, squeeze out the excess water, and let your sponge dry.

To me, the "high" setting felt exactly like treatments I have received in the dr's office. My skin was very smooth and felt wonderful after use. I'm glad I purchased because I get the same result for much less money, not to mention time wasted making weekly appointments. Keep in mind:

*Crystal refills are an additional expense
*The warranty card must be sent in within 10 days of purchase to be valid
*There are different settings so that you can control intensity
